Candlestick Patterns

Illustration for candlestick patterns.

Illustration for candlestick patterns.

Candlesticks summarize open, high, low and close over a stated interval. Common green-up coloring means close above open; the configured colors must be checked. Shape names describe historical observations, not validated forecasts by themselves.

💡
Example

Open 100, high 105, low 99 and close 103 give a body of 3, upper wick of 2, lower wick of 1 and total range of 6. Close 99 instead would describe a down body of 1 using the same open; the shape changes with the actual data.

Doji: open and close are close relative to a chosen tolerance and interval.
Hammer: commonly a small body near the upper end with a longer lower wick; definitions vary.
Engulfing: a multi-candle body comparison, so check whether a definition uses bodies or the full high-low range.
Pro Tip

Label the symbol, source, interval and definition before identifying a shape. Finding a named pattern after a price move does not establish that it could predict the move in advance.

Support & Resistance Levels

Illustration for support & resistance levels.

Support and resistance are analyst-selected areas where past prices have stopped falling or rising. They are not physical barriers or proof of participant intent. Choice of lookback, tolerance and chart scale affects where they are drawn.

💡
Example

Hypothetical closes touch 100, rise to 104, return to 100, then close at 97. Two earlier observations near 100 might motivate a support annotation, but the final observation breaks it. Whether a later return to 100 is called resistance must be checked on later data; it is not an automatic role reversal.

Write the rule before looking at the next observation.
Record failed levels as well as apparent successful reactions.
Compare a zone with a precise line; changing tolerance after the result can overfit the story.
Pro Tip

A drawn level does not place an order. Gaps, execution costs and missing liquidity can make the practice assumption differ from a real fill.

Moving Averages (SMA & EMA)

Illustration for moving averages (sma & ema).

A simple moving average gives equal weight to the selected observations. An exponential moving average gives more weight to recent observations under a specified smoothing rule. Both summarize past data and can lag a change in direction.

💡
Example

Three closes of 100, 102 and 104 have a three-observation SMA of (100 + 102 + 104) ÷ 3 = 102. For a three-period EMA, alpha = 2 ÷ (3 + 1) = 0.5. With a previous EMA of 100 and a new close of 104, the next EMA is 0.5 × 104 + 0.5 × 100 = 102. Initialization affects early values.

A conventional golden cross means the 50-period average crosses above the 200-period average; specify daily or another interval. A death cross is the reverse. These descriptions do not establish a profitable entry or exit, and repeated crossings can occur in sideways data.

Pro Tip

Compare the same series using two lookbacks and keep the time window fixed. Do not choose a setting only because it fits the most favorable past segment.

RSI & MACD Indicators
RSI: relative average gains and losses

Under a common RSI calculation, RSI = 100 − 100 ÷ (1 + average gain / average loss), using a stated lookback and smoothing method. Conventional 70 and 30 thresholds are often called overbought and oversold, but do not guarantee a reversal.

💡
Example

With an average gain of 2 and average loss of 1 in the same units, relative strength is 2 and RSI is about 66.67. A zero average-loss case needs a defined boundary treatment. RSI can remain elevated or depressed through a continuing trend.

MACD: differences between averages
💡
Example

Using the conventional 12/26/9 settings, if the 12-period EMA is 105 and 26-period EMA is 103, MACD is 2. If its signal EMA is 1.5, the histogram is 2 − 1.5 = 0.5. The histogram measures that difference, not the price acceleration itself.

Pro Tip

An indicator divergence compares selected price and indicator observations. It is not proof that a turn is imminent. Document the settings, source and failed examples as well as any apparent signal.
